about.title: About me
about.bio1: I'm a freelance full-stack developer with a strong backend focus. I build web applications and tools — mostly with Go on the server and SvelteKit on the frontend — and I care about systems that are fast, simple, and correct.
about.bio2: My main stack is Go, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, and Docker, with some Python and Rust for the right problems. I tend to go deep before going wide: I'd rather understand why something works than reach for the nearest abstraction.
about.bio3: I studied mathematics up through graduate coursework, which probably explains why I'm drawn to things like consensus algorithms and encryption. Outside of code, I tinker with electronics and play electric guitar.

cluo.overview_1: Built to replace manual investigation workflows. Field agents use a Wails + SvelteKit desktop app for case management, capture evidence on a mobile PWA, and deliver securely to clients through a dedicated portal — all driven by one Go API.
cluo.overview_2: The legal document chain (Estimate → Mandate → Contract → Invoice) is automated as a state machine with per-document PDF generation.
cluo.highlight_1_body: Go API, Wails desktop, mobile PWA, and client portal all share a single hexagonal backend with port interfaces.
cluo.highlight_2_body: transcribes field audio, extracts structured data (people, timelines, facts), and pre-fills the report editor.
cluo.highlight_3_body: Estimate → Mandate → Contract → Invoice modeled as a state machine with per-document PDF generation and delivery.
cluo.highlight_4_body: SHA-256 tokens with configurable expiration and investigator-controlled revocation — no client accounts needed.
cluo.highlight_5_body: Ansible + Terraform for reproducible, version-controlled deployments.

leviosa.overview_1: A crucial component originally built for another project, extracted as a standalone library to facilitate encryption and hashing of sensitive data. The main challenge was designing an API that stays out of the way while remaining correct and fast.

germinal.overview_1: A sophisticated event and talent management platform with bilingual support, media galleries, automated workflows, and production-ready infrastructure.
germinal.overview_2: Built from the ground up as a full-stack showcase demonstrating modern web development practices. The platform features a custom middleware system for cross-cutting concerns, an LRU caching layer with tag-based invalidation, and a PostgreSQL-backed job scheduler for asynchronous tasks.
germinal.highlight_1_body: Decorator pattern for composable request handling — validation, auth, rate limiting, and CSRF in a single chain.
germinal.highlight_2_body: pg-boss integration with cron-scheduled tasks for email queues, cleanup, and reminders.
germinal.highlight_3_body: LRU cache with TTL and tag-based invalidation for optimal performance.
germinal.highlight_4_body: End-to-end TypeScript with Zod schemas for runtime validation.
germinal.highlight_5_body: Multi-stage Docker builds with security hardening (non-root user, Alpine base).
germinal.highlight_6_body: Sentry integration for error tracking and performance monitoring.
germinal.highlight_7_body: Vitest for unit tests and Playwright for E2E coverage.

encx.overview_1: A crucial component of the Cluo project that facilitates encryption and hashing of sensitive data. Designed as a standalone module to avoid becoming a bottleneck in the data pipeline.

vizraft.overview_1: VizRaft is a from-scratch implementation of the Raft distributed consensus algorithm in Go, paired with a real-time visualizer that makes the protocol's behavior tangible. Leader elections, log replication, and network partition recovery all play out visually as you interact with the cluster.
vizraft.overview_2: The goal is to turn a paper into running code, then make that code explainable — both to myself and to anyone trying to understand how distributed systems stay consistent under failure.
